summary: The article provides a generally accurate and helpful guide to recovering unclaimed mutual fund money in India, with most factual claims verified by authoritative sources. However, some tax-related details, particularly regarding recent changes to capital gains tax rates and thresholds, are outdated or inaccurate.

claims.claim: SEBI's Annual Report for FY26 revealed a staggering ₹3,811 crore in unclaimed mutual fund money, including redemption proceeds and dividends.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm this figure from SEBI's FY26 Annual Report.

claims.claim: Post-April 1, 2020, mutual fund dividends are taxable in the hands of the investor as per their income slab.
claims.note: This is correct. Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) was abolished, and dividends became taxable in the hands of the investor from April 1, 2020.

claims.claim: equity funds held for more than one year attract Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year, without indexation.
claims.note: As of July 23, 2024 (and applicable for FY26), LTCG on equity mutual funds exceeding ₹1.25 lakh is taxed at 12.5% without indexation. The ₹1 lakh exemption and 10% rate are outdated.

claims.claim: Short Term Capital Gains (STCG) on equity funds are taxed at 15%.
claims.note: STCG on equity-oriented mutual funds is taxed at 20% if transferred on or after July 23, 2024. It was 15% before this date.

claims.claim: Debt funds have different holding period criteria and tax rates.
claims.note: Taxation for debt funds changed significantly from April 1, 2023. Investments made on or after this date are taxed as short-term capital gains at the investor's slab rate, regardless of the holding period. Older investments (before April 1, 2023) still follow the 3-year holding period for LTCG with indexation.

claims.claim: Mutual fund money can remain unclaimed for many years. AMCs are mandated to hold these funds and make continuous efforts to trace investors. There is generally no specific time limit after which the money lapses to the government, unlike some other financial instruments.
claims.note: Unclaimed mutual fund amounts are transferred to a separate plan (UDRS) after 3 years and continue to earn income. They do not immediately lapse to the government.

claims.claim: No, there are no fees charged by AMCs or RTAs to claim your own unclaimed mutual fund money.
claims.note: Sources confirm that claiming unclaimed amounts from AMCs or RTAs is free of charge.

article_title: Recovering Your Unclaimed Mutual Fund Money in India
